title: Vals AI: independent AI benchmarks for real world tasks
answer: Vals AI publishes independent AI evaluations and benchmarks for real world tasks, including finance, software, cybersecurity and healthcare. Its landing page lists model pricing, context windows and leaderboard results across many benchmarks. For legal readers the most useful detail is that Legal Research appears as a named benchmark in a note about one model's latency, where Hy4 Preview is described as slowest on routine knowledge work such as MedCode, Legal Research and Public Benefits Bench. The page does not set out legal reasoning methods or legal tasks beyond naming Legal Research.

sections.body: Vals AI publishes this page as a landing page for independent AI evaluations and benchmarks on real world tasks. The text says the benchmarks cover finance, software, cybersecurity, healthcare and more. It is not a legal industry report. The supplied text is marked as harvested on 2026-09-29 and consists of model pricing notes, leaderboard positions and short benchmark descriptions. It names benchmarks including the Vals Index, Terminal-Bench 2.1, VoiceCodeBench, CUA-bench, Vibe Code Bench 1-100, Code Migration, Public Benefits Bench, SRE Bench, MedCode and Legal Research.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Vals AI presents itself as an independent evaluator of AI models on real world tasks. The page mixes model specifications, prices and benchmark results. It lists Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Opus 5.5 and Hy4 Preview with token prices, context windows and evaluation settings. It reports that GPT-6 Luna places #20 of 65 on the Vals Index at 58.45% and $0.42 per test, the lowest cost of any model in the top 20 and roughly 18x cheaper than GPT-6 Sol at 62.57% and $7.56. It describes a Claude Opus 5.5 multi agent experiment that produced C-HD, a formally verified improvement over published bounds for exact shortest paths. It introduces CUA-bench, which asks whether an AI agent can play six commercial video games with only a keyboard and a mouse, with one three hour trial per game and no game API, save files or memory inspection. GPT-6 Astra leads at 19.2%, and no model clears a fifth of the suite. No model plays at human speed, acting once every 15 to 59 seconds and sending 2 to 19 inputs a minute. It introduces Vibe Code Bench 1-100, which asks whether a model can evolve a working web application through dependent product requests. It reports Hy4 Preview at #21 of 58 on the Vals Index at 55.40% and $1.28 per test, and says it is slowest on routine knowledge work such as MedCode, Legal Research and Public Benefits Bench.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Vals AI states that GPT-6 Luna places #20 of 65 on the Vals Index at 58.45% and $0.42 per test, roughly 18x cheaper than GPT-6 Sol at 62.57% and $7.56. It states that MiMo V2.6 Flash places #16 of 65 at 59.58% and $0.20 per test, with MiMo V2.6 Pro at #17 and 59.47% and $0.39, both top scoring open weight models ahead of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 57.86% and Kimi K3 at 57.81%. It states that GPT-6 Astra leads CUA-bench at 19.2%, ahead of Claude Fable 5.1 at 13.2%, Claude Opus 5 at 9.0%, GPT-5.6 Sol at 8.3% and Gemini 3.8 Flash at 4.2%, and that no model clears a fifth of the suite. It states that Hy4 Preview places #21 of 58 on the Vals Index at 55.40% and $1.28 per test, and is #4 open weight behind DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3. It states that Hy4 Preview is slowest on routine knowledge work such as MedCode, Legal Research and Public Benefits Bench. It gives model prices including Sonnet 5.5 at $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens, GPT-6 Luna at $0.10 and $0.50, Opus 5.5 at $4.00 and $20.00, and Hy4 Preview at $0.83 and $2.50. It states that Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 has a 2.41s mean time to first partial, on par with GPT Live Transcribe at 2.52s.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Legal would use this source mainly as a pointer to Vals AI's independent benchmark programme, not as a detailed legal reasoning study. The only direct legal signal in the supplied text is that Legal Research is named as a benchmark where Hy4 Preview is slowest on routine knowledge work. The page also shows how Vals AI compares models on cost, latency and task performance, which can help legal AI buyers understand that legal research is one benchmark among many and that speed on routine knowledge work can vary. It does not provide legal specific scores or explain how legal reasoning is tested in the text supplied.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Legal

sections.body: This is a landing page, not a full report or methodology paper. The supplied text is a collection of short model notes and leaderboard snippets. It does not explain how the Legal Research benchmark is built, what tasks it contains, or how models are scored on legal reasoning. It does not give legal specific results for most models. It is commercial in the sense that it promotes Vals AI's evaluations and includes pricing and access details. The text is marked as harvested on 2026-09-29, so it is a snapshot. It covers many industries and benchmarks, so legal readers must treat the legal content as partial.
